chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who enters Mecca once, twice, or four times in a year, what should he do? He said: 'When he enters, let him enter in the state of Talbiyah, and when he leaves, let him leave in the state of Ihram解除 (Muhrim).' He said: 'And for every month, an Umrah.' I said: 'Can it be less?' He said: 'It can be an Umrah for every ten days.' Then he said: 'By your right, indeed in this year of mine, there were six Umrahs.' I said: 'Why is that?' He said: 'I was with Muhammad ibn Ibrahim in al-Ta'if, and whenever he entered, I entered with him.'

key_terms.مُحِلاًّ: In the state of Ihram (ritual consecration) or having concluded the rites, depending on context; here implying the ritual state associated with the pilgrimage rites
key_terms.مُلَبِّياً: In the state of reciting the Talbiyah (chanting 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk') upon entering the Miqat for Umrah

ai.seo_question: How often must a resident of Mecca perform Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in the frequency of Umrah for residents of Mecca, establishing a baseline of one Umrah per month but permitting a reduction to one every ten days. The Imam’s personal practice of performing six Umrahs in a single year while residing in Ta'if serves as a practical precedent (Sunnah) demonstrating that multiple pilgrimages are not only permissible but encouraged for spiritual benefit.
